title: Reverse a word
description: Read a word and print it backwards.
instructions: The program receives one word on a single line. Print the word with its letters in reverse order. Accented and other non-English letters must stay intact. Example: `hello` prints `olleh`.
evaluation_criteria: Works on runes, not bytes, so non-English letters are not broken. Handles one-letter words. No unnecessary variables or libraries.

title: Even or odd
description: Read an integer and say whether it is even or odd.
instructions: The program receives one integer, which may be negative or zero. Print `even` if it is divisible by 2, otherwise print `odd`. Example: `7` prints `odd`.
evaluation_criteria: Uses the remainder operator. Correct for negative numbers and zero. No string conversion.

title: Count the vowels
description: Count how many vowels a line of text contains.
instructions: The program receives one line of text, possibly with spaces. Print how many vowels it contains. The vowels are a, e, i, o and u, in lowercase or uppercase. Example: `Hello World` prints `3`.
evaluation_criteria: Reads the whole line, not just the first word. Counts upper and lower case. Readable loop with no repeated code.

title: Sum of a list
description: Read a list of integers and print their sum.
instructions: The first line holds a number n. The next line holds n integers separated by spaces. Print their sum. The list can be empty (n is 0), and numbers can be negative. Example: `3` then `1 2 3` prints `6`.
evaluation_criteria: Reads exactly n numbers. Handles n = 0 and negative numbers. Uses a running total, not a slice, unless justified.

title: Most frequent word
description: Find the word that appears most often in a line.
instructions: The program receives one line of lowercase words separated by spaces. Print the word that appears most often. If several words are tied, print the one that comes first alphabetically. Example: `the cat and the dog and the bird` prints `the`.
evaluation_criteria: Uses a map to count words. Breaks ties alphabetically in a deterministic way, not by map order. Clear, short code.
